clue.text: It takes continental drivers about an hour, unexpectedly

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist abroad takes roughly an hour longer than planned to complete a drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges ABOUTANH (ABOUT AN plus H). 'about' looks like an approximation but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A German motorway is a road carrying drivers on the European mainland, a cryptic description of its job.

clue.text: Set of instructions that's confusing to a girl meeting Queen

indicators.note: confusing means the letters of the words that follow are mixed up

parts.note: HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A list of directions that a young woman finds baffling when she meets the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusing' is the anagram signal; HM, Her Majesty, is the standard crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: An algorithm is a step-by-step procedure, the sequence of rules a computer follows.

clue.text: Radio covering end of Duchy's harsh regime

indicators.note: covering means the outer word wraps around a letter

parts.note: a tranny is dated British slang for a transistor radio

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Radio coverage about the end of a duchy's cruel government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes Y from Duchy's, and 'covering' puts TRANNY around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyranny is cruel and oppressive rule, the government of a despot.

clue.text: Girl's bottom fitting into inappropriate underwear

indicators.note: fitting into means one piece slots inside the other

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear; with something in it that should not be there it is inappropriate
the end is the bottom of something

explanation.surface: A girl's backside fitting into underwear that is unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting into' puts END inside BRA. The 's of Girl's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a female first name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Has bonnet with flashes

parts.note: hood and bonnet are both head coverings, and also car parts
winks are quick flashes of light, as in a winking light

explanation.surface: Someone owns a bonnet that has flashing lights on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like the verb of owning but means tricks, as in 'you've been had'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone is slang for to trick or deceive them, as is hoodwink.

clue.text: Isle of Man area

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to name the Isle of Man, the self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isle of Man' reads as a single place name, but the definition stops at 'Isle'; 'Man' is a verb. STAFFA is the small Hebridean island with Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffa is a small uninhabited island in the Inner Hebrides of Scotland, so an example of an island.

clue.text: A vast, or sprawling, Russian city

indicators.note: sprawling means spread out untidily, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A vast, sprawling Russian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sprawling' rearranges AVASTOR. The words look like a description of the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Saratov is a large city on the Volga river in southern Russia.

clue.text: A hand put up, defending Conservative's style of music

indicators.note: defending means the outer word protects, surrounds, the letter

parts.note: to give a hand is to give aid, help
C is the abbreviation for Conservative; the 's is a link
to put someone up is to house them for the night

explanation.surface: A hand raised in defence of the Conservatives' taste in music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defending' puts C inside AID. 'put up' looks like raising a hand, but means to house.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid house is a form of electronic dance music from the late 1980s.

clue.text: Mix airmen up with gunners on leave

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: An instruction to mix aircrew with artillerymen while they are on leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAF into FAR. 'Mix' looks like a verb but is the noun, a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch, a mixture.

clue.text: Bring a rod to catch it?

definitions.text: Bring a rod to catch it?

indicators.note: to catch means the letters are held inside the words that come before

explanation.surface: Advice to an angler: take a fishing rod if you want to land one.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'brinG A Rod'; the whole clue also describes the fish, since you would bring a rod to catch a gar.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar or garfish is a long-snouted fish, and anglers use rods to catch fish.

clue.text: Note short Noel Riordan disposing of Dan Green in a fight?

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off the surname

parts.note: Noel Coward was the English playwright and songwriter

indicators.note: disposing of tells us to throw these letters out of the name before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Noel Riordan seems to be getting rid of a man named Dan Green in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims COWARD to COWAR; 'disposing of' removes DAN from RIORDAN to leave RIOR. 'Dan Green' looks like a name, but 'Green' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An environmental activist who campaigns combatively is a green, or ecologist, engaged in a struggle.

clue.text: Call room service, perhaps, to do something with curtain

definitions.meaning: to telephone downstairs to the hotel desk or kitchen from your room
in a theatre, to lower the curtain at the end of a performance

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both phoning down from a room and lowering a stage curtain, two set expressions.

clue.text: Come again in coach after one's left Asian city

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second
left means this letter has departed from the word

parts.note: a coach is a railway carriage, a train
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link
come again? is a request to repeat, like eh?

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a repeat while on a coach journey after a fellow passenger has got off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes the one, leaving TRAN; 'in' is the container signal. 'Come again' reads as a return visit but is the query 'eh?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Iran is a city in Asia, so the clue names a type the answer belongs to.

clue.text: Fiddles first parts of seven year old tax return

indicators.note: return as in sending back means the selected letters are read backwards
first parts of means take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A seven-year-old child fiddling a tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'seven year old tax' are SYOT, which 'return' turns round. 'tax return' looks like a phrase but 'return' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to fiddle with it idly, so both are verbs of fidgeting.

clue.text: Careless using cuff, unlike a lot of policemen?

parts.note: a cuff is a blow with the open hand, a slap
Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance says a policeman's lot is not a happy one, so something unlike it is happy

explanation.surface: Someone casual about lashing out with their hand, not like most police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark points to the song from The Pirates of Penzance: 'A policeman's lot is not a happy one'. 'lot' looks like 'many' but means fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap-happy means cheerfully casual and careless, as well as dazed from blows.

clue.text: Run off via rocks, overtaking old pro

indicators.note: overtaking suggests one thing taking in another as it passes, so a letter goes inside
on the rocks means in disarray, so the words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner leaves via some rocks and passes an old professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges RUNOFFVIA and 'overtaking' takes O inside it. 'pro' looks like a noun but here means for, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pro something means supporting it, the same as being on its side.

clue.text: Upon quick butcher's cut a label is superimposed

indicators.note: superimposed means placed on top, and in a down entry that means written first

parts.note: a tag is a label
to lance is to cut, as a boil

explanation.surface: A butcher quickly cuts meat and puts a label on top.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is rhyming slang: butcher's hook, look. 'is superimposed' puts A TAG above LANCE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something in with a brief look is what the phrase means, matching a quick look.

clue.text: Check tip of prop thoroughly

indicators.note: to tip something over is to turn it, so the short word is turned back to front

parts.note: a rest is a support, like the snooker cue rest
all means completely, as in all wet

explanation.surface: Advice to inspect the end of a propeller carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' turns OF into FO. It reads as a noun, the end of the prop, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to prevent or block it in advance, to check it.

clue.text: Island hopping, a vehicle needs to take in fuel

parts.note: hopping mad means furious, so hopping alone means angry

indicators.note: to take in means the vehicle holds the fuel inside

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
gas is fuel, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Someone touring islands finds their vehicle needs to be filled up with fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopping' suggests island-hopping but means angry, as in hopping mad; 'to take in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Madagascar is the large island off the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Roman general gets a firm hold, a year later

indicators.note: later means this piece follows the earlier ones

parts.note: a grip is a firm hold
p.a. stands for per annum, a year

explanation.surface: A Roman general getting a firm grip on things, a year on.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is per annum, Latin for each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was a Roman general and Augustus's right-hand man, victor at Actium.

clue.text: Love to enter offering practical experience in the East End, etc

indicators.note: to enter means this letter goes inside the phrase
Cockneys of London's East End drop their aitches, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: hands-on describes direct practical experience
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A love of offering practical training in London's East End, and so forth.
explanation.walkthrough: London's East End Cockney accent drops the letter H, which 'in the East End' signals, leaving 'ANDSON; 'to enter' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc. is short for et cetera, meaning the same as 'and the rest'.

clue.text: For good wicket replacing very short pitcher

indicators.note: replacing means one letter is swapped in where another stood

parts.note: for ever means for good, permanently
very cut short leaves its first letter
W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket

explanation.surface: A cricket clue: a wicket for good, and a very short pitcher, as if describing a bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' puts W for V in EVER. 'pitcher' and 'wicket' suggest cricket or baseball, but the pitcher is a jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large water jug, a vessel for pouring, which is what a pitcher is.

clue.text: Club to stop filming picture

parts.note: a wood is a golf club
cut! is the director's call to stop filming

explanation.surface: A golf club used to stop the filming of a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' suggests a film after 'filming', but here it is a print.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodcut is a print made from a carved block of wood, a kind of picture.

clue.text: City put up with what Brighton has to go through

indicators.note: with means the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: Brighton, the English seaside resort, has a famous pier

indicators.note: in a down entry, put up means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: A city erected alongside Brighton's attraction, something to pass through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns EC into CE. Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast, known for its pier.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to go through something, puncturing it.

clue.text: Vaulted river (did long crossing)

indicators.note: crossing means the second piece goes across, inside, the first

parts.note: ached means longed, as in ached for something

explanation.surface: A vaulted chamber beside a river that someone took a long time to cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside ACHED. 'Vaulted' looks like the past tense of jumping but means built with a curved roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaulted roof is one built with a curved shape, which is what arched describes.

clue.text: Wrong number one's ringing I state

parts.note: ill means wrong, as in ill-advised

indicators.note: ringing means the outer letters encircle the others

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: Someone dialled a wrong number and the person whose phone is ringing is me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' puts NO and I inside I and S. 'Wrong number' and 'ringing' make a telephone picture, but 'ringing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is one of the United States, a Midwestern state with Chicago its largest city.

clue.text: Practice match seed always needs to clinch tournament

parts.note: a pip is a fruit seed

indicators.note: to clinch means to hold tightly, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always
an open is a tournament anyone may enter, like the British Open

explanation.surface: A tennis or golf seed who always needs to win a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to clinch' signals the container. 'seed' looks like a tournament ranking but means a fruit pip.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe-opener is a warm-up exercise or preliminary bout, a practice before the real contest.

clue.text: Bill returns clutching hot drink

indicators.note: clutching means the outer letters hold the other one
returns means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: AC is an abbreviation for account, a bill
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Bill comes back carrying a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns AC into CA, and 'clutching' puts H inside it. 'Bill' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is British slang for tea, a hot drink, from the Chinese word.

clue.text: Tin that makes you gorge

parts.note: a tin is a can
yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A can of food so tempting it makes you eat greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a verb, to stuff oneself, but is the noun for a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep narrow valley with steep sides, the same as a gorge.

clue.text: Work cycle's got established inside base

indicators.note: inside means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: to pedal is to work a bicycle; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A work cycle has become established inside a company base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' signals the container. 'Work cycle' reads as a routine, but means to ride a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the support at the bottom of a column or statue, its base.
